intended_object: The rotation by angle θ acting on G ⊕ G ≅ ℝ² ⊗ G for a real vector space G, i.e. the block matrix [[cos θ, −sin θ],[sin θ, cos θ]] applied to pairs (x₁, x₂), as a real-linear automorphism. Inferred from the docstring and from its use in the library, which builds a linear isometry on `WithLp 2 (G × G)` from it.
explanation:
The forward map is (x₁, x₂) ↦ (cos θ·x₁ − sin θ·x₂, sin θ·x₁ + cos θ·x₂), which is the standard rotation matrix. The inverse map is (x₁, x₂) ↦ (cos θ·x₁ + sin θ·x₂, −sin θ·x₁ + cos θ·x₂), which is rotation by −θ, the correct inverse. Both are ℝ-linear.

The setting is natural. Real scalars are the standard setting for rotation by a real angle. G only needs to be a real module, which is the most general setting where cos θ and sin θ act as scalars. One could abstract to any ring with a pair (c, s) satisfying c² + s² = 1, but that is no longer "rotation by θ".

Mathlib has related notions, `Orientation.rotation` (for oriented 2-dimensional inner product spaces) and rotations in ℂ. Neither is this rotation on G × G for an arbitrary real module G, so there is no more general Mathlib definition to point to.
